title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

ideas.what: Schematic picture of a conformal surface or disc with marked points (punctures), each with a small disc or collar neighbourhood, one with a larger annular neighbourhood (tentative interpretation)
ideas.modern_name: Cusp / collar neighbourhoods; plumbing coordinates near punctures (Deligne–Mumford boundary, Fenchel–Nielsen / Earle–Marden plumbing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Collar lemma: Keen, Halpern, Buser. Plumbing coordinates: Kra, Earle–Marden, Wolpert. Tate uniformisation: Tate.
ideas.where_published: The general theme of gluing surfaces and cutting along curves near punctures appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in its discussion of Teichmüller towers and 'surgery' of surfaces. This specific sketch is not published.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused envelope carrying only an address and two unlabelled doodles of discs with marked points. It has no statement, computation or construction, so there is nothing missed by the literature. Its only value is as context for the surgery and annulus computations on the adjacent pages.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially correct. Handwritten address: 'M. Grothendieck'. Printed sender: UNIVERSITE DES SCIENCES ET TECHNIQUES DU LANGUEDOC / INSTITUT DE MATHEMATIQUES / Place Eugène Bataillon / 34060 MONTPELLIER CEDEX (a small orange/brown mark partly covers the 'C' of CEDEX).
There is a pencilled archival folio number '9' in the lower-left corner.
In the lower drawing, the inner circle contains a filled dot plus a small extra mark (possibly a second tiny dot or tick). The two small circled dots sit at right and bottom inside the large circle.
